# CanvasDesk

> Visual mathematical modeling system: an infinite canvas where models assembled from Numi formula sheets and 45 calculation templates compute themselves. Values flow along value-edges and the whole chain recalculates instantly. Open source (AGPL-3.0), written in Rust, web version on WebGPU.

CanvasDesk replaces the "Miro + Excel + Google Docs + PowerPoint" stack for mathematical modeling. Built-in domain math: Erlang-C and M/M/1 (service capacity), NPV, cohort LTV (unit economics), retention and funnels (product analytics). Bottlenecks (ρ ≥ 1) light up on the canvas; what-if scenarios show was → became (+Δ) deltas. An AI agent can assemble and verify models via MCP: 39 tools including graph_apply and graph_validate, started with one command (`canvasdesk mcp`). Engine benchmarks: 1000-node graph recalculates in under 10 ms; 5000 nodes at 60 FPS.

## Web app

- [CanvasDesk Web](https://danku13.github.io/CanvasDesk/app/): runs in Chrome/Edge, no sign-up required; models are stored locally in the browser.

## Documentation

- [Docs](https://danku13.github.io/CanvasDesk/): getting started, file format, MCP setup.

## Limitations (as stated by the author)

- Web version: Chrome/Edge only (WebGPU); Firefox is experimental.
- Linux and macOS builds ship the windowed canvas; some desktop features (file thumbnails, drag-and-drop, MCP) are Windows-only for now.
